lead.label: 3h
lead.why: Abstract: 'compound 3f (IC50 = 1.05) and 3h (IC50 = 0.96 uM) exhibited potent inhibition of PKM2, superior to 3k and shikonin'; the abstract names two, 3h has the lowest IC50 (most potent). 3f was the one used as 'representative compound' for the normal-cell cytotoxicity test, so 3f is the alternative reading; its route is identical with thiomorpholine in place of thiazolidine.

reactions.conditions: 1,4-naphthoquinone (1 g, 6.3 mmol) in glacial AcOH (20 mL), 36% aq. HCHO (6 mL), ice-water cooling, dry HCl passed 2 h, then rt 48 h; poured on ice, EtOAc extraction, column; 68.9%.
reactions.source: main text p.3 'Procedure for preparation of 2,3-bis-chloromethyl-[1,4]naphthoquinone (2)'

reactions.conditions: General procedure: CS2 (3 mmol) and amine (3 mmol) in MeCN (5 mL), 30 min; 2 (1 mmol) added in portions; rt 48 h; concentrated, H2O/CH2Cl2 extraction, column (PE/CH2Cl2); 88.8% for 3h.
reactions.source: main text p.3 'General procedure for preparation of ... (3a-3h)' and data for 3h

notes: The amine for 3h is not printed as a stand-alone name; 'thiazolidinyl' (R column, results text) and the NMR (12H, 2 NCH2CH2SCH2) fix it as thiazolidin-3-yl. Printed names are the paper's own non-IUPAC style and may not parse in OPSIN. Two equivalents of CS2, amine, HCHO and HCl are incorporated (listed twice). Lead choice between 3f and 3h is a near tie (IC50 1.05 vs 0.96); 3h chosen as the lowest IC50; 3f (thiomorpholine, SMILES O=C1C(CSC(=S)N2CCSCC2)=C(CSC(=S)N2CCSCC2)C(=O)c2ccccc12) shares the same two-step route.
